question: Who among the following social reformers developed the modern Bengali Alphabet in British India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar** was a prominent social reformer, educationist, and writer of the 19th century in British India.
 
• He played a key role in the development of the **modern Bengali alphabet** and its rationalization, making it simpler and more accessible.
 
• Vidyasagar introduced **typographical standardization** of Bengali script, which included the introduction of punctuation and elimination of redundant characters.
 
• His work on Bengali grammar and script greatly influenced the **modernization of the Bengali language** and its usage in literature and education.
 
• He is also remembered for his contributions to **women’s education and widow remarriage** in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bengali Alphabet**

 
 
• The Bengali script is derived from the ancient **Brahmi script**, and its development was influenced by the Nagari and Siddham scripts.
 
• The modern Bengali alphabet consists of **11 vowels** and **39 consonants**.
 
• Vidyasagar’s contributions helped standardize the script, making it suitable for printing and education.
 
 
 
• **Social Reforms by Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar**
 
 
• He was a staunch advocate for the **widow remarriage movement** in India, leading to the passage of the Widow Remarriage Act of 1856.
 
• Vidyasagar worked tirelessly to promote **education for women** and established schools dedicated to their upliftment.
 
 
 
• **His Contributions to Literature and Education**
 
 
• Vidyasagar authored *‘Borno Porichoy’*, a book that simplified Bengali grammar and script for children.
 
• He was instrumental in **modernizing the education system** in Bengal by introducing Western methodologies and rational thinking.
 
 
 
• **Legacy**
 
 
• Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar is fondly remembered as the **“Father of Bengali Prose”** for his contributions to the language.
 
• He is also regarded as one of the key architects of the Bengal Renaissance, which marked a period of cultural and intellectual awakening in 19th-century India.
